Chapter 8: Deepening the Relationship with Symbols
As we move forward on this journey, you might notice a longing to go deeper—to move past the surface and really connect with the symbols that mean the most to you.
This isn’t just about studying or memorizing meanings. It’s about presence. About letting your chosen symbols become living companions in your daily life.
One beautiful way to deepen this relationship is through creative practice. Imagine spending an afternoon sketching or painting a symbol you love—letting your hand and heart guide you, with no set plan.
As you do, the act of creating becomes a kind of meditation. You might notice unexpected emotions—maybe a sudden joy, a wave of sadness, or even a burst of fresh inspiration.
In these moments, your symbol turns into a doorway, inviting you to discover new parts of yourself.
For others, meaning unfolds through ritual. Picture lighting a candle for someone close to your heart, arranging stones in a circle, or slipping on a necklace etched with a special symbol.
These small, everyday acts become ways to honor what truly matters to you. Over time, the rituals take on their own life—marking the rhythms of your days, the changing seasons, even the passing years.
Some people choose to invite symbols into their dreams. Before bed, they might tuck a symbol under their pillow or take a few quiet moments just visualizing it.
In the morning, they reflect on any images or feelings that surfaced overnight. The symbol becomes a gentle guide, helping you navigate the mysterious landscape of your unconscious mind.
Journaling is another powerful way to connect. Maybe you keep a notebook just for your symbols—jotting down when and where they show up, what they seem to mean, and how you feel in those moments.
Over time, you’ll start to notice patterns. Maybe a certain symbol appears whenever you’re stressed, or right before you make a big decision. Your journal starts to look like a map, charting your growth and transformation.
For some, the relationship with symbols is deeply personal—almost secret. You might carry a small token in your pocket, reaching for it in moments of doubt or fear.
That symbol becomes a quiet source of strength, a reminder that you’re never truly alone.
Others love to share their symbols with friends or family, creating a kind of shared language. Maybe a group of friends each picks a symbol for the year, checking in as the months go by.
The symbols become a way to support each other, celebrate milestones, and weather tough times together.
What really stands out is this: your relationship with symbols is always changing, always growing.
There’s no right or wrong way to connect. The most important thing is to listen—to let your symbols speak, to honor the feelings they stir, and to trust the wisdom they gently offer.
